html:
The Sanctuary of Aphrodite Paphia was a great shrine of the goddess Aphrodite at Old Paphos, today's Kouklia in southwest Cyprus, used from about 1200 BCE until pagan cults were banned in the late 300s CE.

Greek myth said Aphrodite was born from the sea foam near Paphos, and Homer calls her the Cyprian. She was worshipped here not as a statue but as a cone shaped black stone, a sign of older Near Eastern fertility cults. Pilgrims came from all over the Greek and Roman world, and the priest kings of Paphos ran the shrine. The Roman emperor Titus visited it. After Christianity became the state religion under Theodosius, the sanctuary was abandoned. It is part of a World Heritage Site.
